meta.title: Personal data breach: report or not?
meta.description: A UK GDPR decision tree for the data protection officer: four questions decide whether to report a breach within 72 hours and whether to tell the people affected.

summary.headline: Report to the regulator within 72 hours unless the breach is unlikely to put anyone at risk; tell the people affected when the risk is high.
points: The 72 hours run from when you become aware of the breach, not from when the investigation ends.
A processor does not report to the regulator; it tells the controller without undue delay.
Every breach goes in the internal breach log, reported or not, with the reasons for the decision.

data.title: Is personal data involved?
data.subtitle: Anything that identifies a living person

data.title: Was it lost, exposed or changed?
data.subtitle: Or accessed or made unavailable
data.description: A breach covers accidents as well as attacks: an email to the wrong person, a lost laptop, ransomware that locks records.

data.title: Security incident only
data.subtitle: Follow the incident process
data.description: No personal data means no GDPR breach. Handle it under the normal security incident process.

data.title: Are we the controller?
data.subtitle: We decide why the data is used

data.title: Near miss
data.subtitle: Log it and fix the weakness

data.title: How likely is harm to people?
data.subtitle: Fraud, distress, discrimination, loss
data.description: Weigh the type of data, how much of it, who could now see it and whether it was encrypted.

data.title: Tell the controller
data.subtitle: Without undue delay
data.description: As a processor, tell the client who controls the data straight away and give them what they need to decide.

data.title: Record, do not report
data.subtitle: Breach log with the reasoning
data.description: For example, encrypted data on a lost device whose key was not lost. Write down why harm is unlikely.

data.title: Report to the regulator
data.subtitle: Within 72 hours of awareness
data.description: Report what is known now and add detail later; explain any delay beyond 72 hours.

data.title: Report and tell people
data.subtitle: Regulator in 72 hours, people now
data.description: Report to the regulator and send the people affected a plain-language notice: what happened, the likely consequences and what they can do.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Start at the top as soon as an incident is raised. Red cards have a 72-hour deadline, amber means tell someone, teal means record it.

steps.title: Is it a personal data breach?
steps.description: It is when personal data was lost, exposed, changed, accessed or made unavailable, by accident or on purpose. Anything else is logged elsewhere.

steps.title: Whose duty is it?
steps.description: Only the controller reports. A processor's duty is to tell its controller quickly.

steps.title: The 72-hour test
steps.description: If harm is unlikely, record the breach and the reasons. If it is likely, report to the regulator within 72 hours.

steps.title: High risk: tell the people too
steps.description: Exposed bank details or health records are high risk: report and tell the individuals directly so they can protect themselves.
